title: Sequential DG colimits with their canonical telescope legs
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A differential graded algebra over $\mathbf Z$ means an associative unital graded ring $A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}A^i$ with additive differential $d:A^i\to A^{i+1}$ satisfying $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^ia\,d(b)$ for $a\in A^i$. A right differential graded $A$-module is a graded right module $M$ with $d^2=0$ and $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^jm\,d(a)$ for $m\in M^j$. Write $D(A,d)$ for the homotopy category of these modules localized at the maps inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology groups; triangles are the distinguished mapping-cone triangles. Let $(P_m,v_m:P_m\to P_{m+1})_{m\in\mathbf N}$ be a sequence of right differential graded $A$-modules. Let $P=\operatorname{colim}_mP_m$ be their degreewise module colimit, with induced differential and canonical maps $j_m:P_m\to P$. The category $D(A,d)$ has all small coproducts, represented by direct sums of differential graded modules. In $D(A,d)$ there is a distinguished triangle $$\bigoplus_mP_m\xrightarrow{1-s}\bigoplus_mP_m\xrightarrow{j}P\longrightarrow(\bigoplus_mP_m)[1],\qquad s\iota_m=\iota_{m+1}v_m,\quad j\iota_m=j_m.$$ Thus the specified canonical legs make $P$ a homotopy colimit in the sense of [def-kun-truncations]. No injectivity assumption on the transition maps is imposed.

proof.text: For complexes of abelian groups, cohomology commutes with degreewise direct sums and products: cycles are coordinatewise cycles, and a family of boundaries has coordinatewise primitives. In a direct sum choose primitives only on its finite support; in a product choose a primitive in every coordinate. Thus the boundaries are the direct sum, respectively product, of the boundary groups. Taking representatives of cohomology classes in the same way proves $H^r(\bigoplus_i C_i)=\bigoplus_i H^r(C_i)$ and $H^r(\prod_i C_i)=\prod_i H^r(C_i)$. These identifications commute with coordinate maps. In particular, sums of quasi-isomorphisms are quasi-isomorphisms and products of acyclic complexes are acyclic.

source.place: Tag 09QI, lemma-derived-products: coordinate calculations for the Hom-complex argument; written out here.

proof.text:
Let $(M_i)_{i\in I}$ be any small family of right DG $A$-modules. Regard $A$ as the one-object dg category with endomorphism complex $A$ and composition $a\circ b=ab$; by the DG Leibniz rule this is a dg category, and its right dg modules, Hom complexes, cohomology and shifts are those of this item, with representable module $A$. By [lem-coef-dg-module-semi-free-replacement] choose quasi-isomorphisms $q_i:Q_i\to M_i$ with $Q_i$ semi-free; by [lem-coef-dg-semi-free-homotopically-projective] each $Q_i$ is homotopically projective. The degreewise sums $Q=\bigoplus_iQ_i$ and $M=\bigoplus_iM_i$ have coordinatewise differential and action. Restriction to summands identifies the complexes $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(Q,N)=\prod_i\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(Q_i,N)$: homogeneous module maps out of a sum correspond to their restrictions, and the Hom differential is computed coordinatewise. For acyclic $N$ every factor is acyclic, so step 1 makes $Q$ homotopically projective; $q=\bigoplus_iq_i:Q\to M$ is a quasi-isomorphism by step 1. By [lem-sfb-dg-homotopically-projective-hom-derived], applied to $Q$ and to each $Q_i$, the localization functor induces bijections $H^0\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(Q,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A,d)}(Q,N)$ and $H^0\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(Q_i,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A,d)}(Q_i,N)$. Taking $H^0$, using step 1 for products, and inverting $q,q_i$ therefore gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A,d)}(M,N)\cong H^0\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(Q,N)\cong\prod_i H^0\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(Q_i,N)\cong\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A,d)}(M_i,N).$$
The components are restriction along the actual summand inclusions, because the localization functor respects composition and $q\iota_i=\iota_iq_i$. This is exactly the coproduct universal property, including the empty family.

proof.text: Put $B=\bigoplus_mP_m$ as a DG module. Define $f=1-s$ by $f\iota_m=\iota_m-\iota_{m+1}v_m$, and define $j:B\to P$ by $j\iota_m=j_m$. These are DG maps and $jf=0$, since all $v_m,j_m$ commute with the differential and action and $j_{m+1}v_m=j_m$. In each degree $f(x)=0$ implies $x_0=0$ and $x_m=v_{m-1}(x_{m-1})$ for $m\geq1$, hence $x=0$ by induction; no $v_m$ is assumed injective. The cokernel of $f$ is the quotient of $\bigoplus_mP_m$ by $\iota_m(x)=\iota_{m+1}(v_mx)$. A homomorphism out of this quotient is precisely a family $a_m$ with $a_{m+1}v_m=a_m$; iteration gives compatibility with every transition. This is the defining universal property of the degreewise colimit, and its quotient map is $j$. Hence $0\to B\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{j}P\to0$ is degreewise exact as a sequence of complexes of abelian groups. The differential and homogeneous right actions preserve these relations, so these are the stated DG-module colimit and maps.

proof.text: Use the right DG cone $C(f)=B\oplus B[1]$, with unchanged graded right action on the shifted summand and differential $d(y,x)=(d_By+f(x),-d_Bx)$. The DG Leibniz identity follows by substituting this formula and the identity for $B$, since $f$ is $A$-linear. Define $c:C(f)\to P$ by $c(y,x)=j(y)$. It is $A$-linear, and $c\,d(y,x)=j(d_By+f(x))=d_Pj(y)$ because $jf=0$, so it is a DG map. On underlying complexes of abelian groups this is exactly the canonical map of [lem-pc-cone-short-exact-quasi-iso] for the short exact sequence in step 3. That node therefore makes $c$ a quasi-isomorphism. DG quasi-isomorphisms are detected on these same underlying cohomology groups, so $c$ is inverted in $D(A,d)$. Moreover, for the cone inclusion $i:B\to C(f)$, one has $ci=j$ already as DG maps.

source.place: Tag 09L0, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor and its preceding cone construction; Tag 0CRL, lemma-homotopy-colimit.

proof.text: By the mapping-cone definition of distinguished triangles in $D(A,d)$, $B\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{i}C(f)\xrightarrow{\delta}B[1]$ is distinguished. The triangle with third object $P$, second arrow $j$ and last arrow $\delta c^{-1}$ is isomorphic to it through $(1_B,1_B,c)$, using $ci=j$, and is therefore distinguished. Step 2 identifies both copies of $B$ with the required derived coproduct and their original inclusions with its coprojections. Consequently its first map satisfies $f\iota_m=\iota_m-\iota_{m+1}v_m$ and its second satisfies $j\iota_m=j_m$. These are the specified legs, so the triangle is precisely a homotopy-colimit triangle as defined in [def-kun-truncations].
